title: Step 6: Ship the Tool
story: Make it a command-line tool: logs in from stdin, report out.
goal: Read all lines from input and print the report.
starter: # read stdin lines, then print the report

tests.label: Parses every line
tests.expr:
len(parse_all('2025-01-05 10:00:01 INFO server started
2025-01-05 10:00:07 ERROR disk full
2025-01-05 10:01:00 WARN slow query

2025-01-05 10:02:11 ERROR disk full
2025-01-05 10:03:09 ERROR timeout
2025-01-05 10:04:00 INFO request ok'))

tests.label: Counts levels
tests.expr:
count_levels(parse_all('2025-01-05 10:00:01 INFO server started
2025-01-05 10:00:07 ERROR disk full
2025-01-05 10:01:00 WARN slow query

2025-01-05 10:02:11 ERROR disk full
2025-01-05 10:03:09 ERROR timeout
2025-01-05 10:04:00 INFO request ok'))

tests.label: Most common error first
tests.expr:
top_errors(parse_all('2025-01-05 10:00:01 INFO server started
2025-01-05 10:00:07 ERROR disk full
2025-01-05 10:01:00 WARN slow query

2025-01-05 10:02:11 ERROR disk full
2025-01-05 10:03:09 ERROR timeout
2025-01-05 10:04:00 INFO request ok'), 2)

tests.label: Limit respected
tests.expr:
top_errors(parse_all('2025-01-05 10:00:01 INFO server started
2025-01-05 10:00:07 ERROR disk full
2025-01-05 10:01:00 WARN slow query

2025-01-05 10:02:11 ERROR disk full
2025-01-05 10:03:09 ERROR timeout
2025-01-05 10:04:00 INFO request ok'), 1)

tests.label: Report text
tests.expr:
report('2025-01-05 10:00:01 INFO server started
2025-01-05 10:00:07 ERROR disk full
2025-01-05 10:01:00 WARN slow query

2025-01-05 10:02:11 ERROR disk full
2025-01-05 10:03:09 ERROR timeout
2025-01-05 10:04:00 INFO request ok')

tests.label: Prints the report from stdin
tests.expect:
ERROR: 3
INFO: 2
WARN: 1
Top error: disk full (2)

hints: Read lines with input() until EOFError.
Join the lines with newlines and pass them to report().
socratic: What should this new piece take in, and give back?
Which earlier piece can you reuse?
Compare your output with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: how does this checkpoint build on the last one?
